english: Those Manichaeans with whom we no longer share communion—that is, all those with whom we disagree—say that free will was lost through the sin of the first man, Adam. They say that no one now has the power to live well, and that everyone is forced into sin by the necessity of their flesh.
translator_notes: Julian is describing and attacking his opponents' teaching here; he is not endorsing the position he attributes to them. Augustine disputes this description.

english: They also say that the marriages now taking place were not instituted by God. This can be read in Augustine's book, which I have just answered in four short books. Our enemies have adopted Augustine's statements out of hatred for the truth.
translator_notes: The book Julian attacks is Augustine's On Marriage and Concupiscence, Book 1. Augustine denies that Julian has described its teaching correctly.

english: They also say that the movement of the sexual organs and the intercourse of married couples were devised by the devil. For that reason, they say, people who are born innocent are guilty and are made by the devil rather than by God, because they are born from this diabolical intercourse. This is unmistakably Manichaean.
translator_notes: These are Julian's accusations against his opponents, which Augustine rejects.

english: They say that the saints of the Old Testament were not free from sins: that is, even by correcting their lives they were not freed from wrongdoing, but death overtook them while they were still guilty.
They say that even the apostle Paul, and indeed all the apostles, were continually defiled by uncontrolled sexual desire.
translator_notes: Augustine connects this accusation to the interpretation of Romans 7:18 and its surrounding argument. That Bible reference is Augustine's explanation of the dispute, not an explicit citation in Julian's surviving sentence.

english: [They say that] even Christ was not free from sins, but was driven by the necessity of the flesh to lie and was stained by other offenses.
translator_notes: Augustine reports this as something Julian accused Augustine's side of saying. It is not Julian's confession about Christ, and Augustine denies having taught it. The opening words in square brackets make that reported accusation explicit.

english: They also say that baptism does not grant complete forgiveness of sins or remove wrongdoing, but merely shaves it away, leaving the roots of all sins in the evil flesh.
translator_notes: Julian again describes his opponents' alleged view. Augustine explicitly denies the shaving analogy.

english: We argue against these things every day. We refuse to agree with those who do wrong, because we say that free will belongs to everyone by nature and could not have been destroyed by Adam's sin. The authority of all the Scriptures confirms this.
translator_notes: Julian refers broadly to Scripture without identifying a particular passage in the preserved wording.

english: We say that the marriages now taking place throughout the world were instituted by God. Married people are not guilty; it is those who commit sexual immorality and adultery who should be condemned.
We say that the movement of the sexual organs—that is, the male sexual capacity itself, without which intercourse cannot take place—was instituted by God.
translator_notes: The Latin word translated 'male sexual capacity' is virilitas; the immediate subject is the bodily capacity needed for intercourse.

english: We maintain that human beings are God's work. His power does not force anyone against their will into either evil or good. People do good or evil by their own will. In a good action they are always helped by God's grace; toward evil they are urged by the devil's suggestions.

We say that the saints of the Old Testament passed from this life to eternal life with their righteousness perfected. That is, through devotion to virtue they had turned away from all sins. For even those whom we read of as having committed some sin, we know to have corrected themselves afterward.
We confess that Christ's grace is necessary for everyone, adults and infants alike. We condemn those who say that a child born to two baptized parents does not need to be baptized.
translator_notes: 'Condemn' translates anathematizamus: a formal rejection of the stated teaching, not merely personal disagreement.

english: We also condemn those who say that baptism does not wipe away all sins, because we know that these mysteries grant complete cleansing.

Let no one deceive you, then, and let the ungodly not deny that they hold these opinions. If they are telling the truth, either let us have a hearing, or let these very bishops who now disagree condemn the positions which, as I have said above, they hold along with the Manichaeans—just as we condemn the things they allege against us. Then there will be complete agreement. If they refuse, know that they are Manichaeans, and refrain from sharing fellowship with them.
translator_notes: 'Let no one deceive you' may echo the biblical warning in Ephesians 5:6 or 1 John 3:7; the wording alone does not establish a definite allusion to either passage.
